claim: Some Blood community maps are conversions of Duke levels and say nothing about Blood: knowledge/blood/duke-conversions.json finds ten, seven of them Duke's E1L1 (E1L1.MAP, Duke1, HollHolo, FORDTHEA with 139 of its sectors matching the Duke level, Intime~2, AFTSHOCK with 71, melte1m1), so FORDTHEA is not a Blood theatre exemplar. Several maps sharing one source are one witness, not several. In our work exemplars of a room were found by scanning every map for its parts and rendering the leads, not by file name.
evidence: The owner, 2026-11-23: 'AFTSHOCK is actually conversion of E1L1 map from Duke3D'; knowledge/blood/duke-conversions.json made by tools/find_duke_conversions.py lists them.

knowledge/blood/duke-conversions.json conversions: community/FORDTHEA.MAP duke E1L1.MAP, sectors 139, share_of_duke_level 0.43; `sectors` there is how many of the map's sectors match the Duke level (duke_conversions.py:64-70), not how many the map has (rerun 2026-11-26 over the corpus's 1,587 readable campaign, curated and community maps)
use: Check each lead against knowledge/blood/duke-conversions.json before treating it as Blood practice.

checked.how: Reran python -m tools.find_duke_conversions (now over bloodmap.corpus: 1,587 Blood maps against 1,504 by the old glob, which missed community subfolders): the same 10 conversions, 7 of E1L1; FORDTHEA 139 sectors matching (share 0.43), AFTSHOCK 71 (0.22); `sectors` counts the map's sectors that match the Duke level. The owner's words of 2026-11-23 are in the file's rule.
